notes: Authored corpus for the real_remote_work quality case. The documents are written for this evaluation, not copied from published sources: the writer's names, venues and DOIs are fictional. Their value is that they are full-length prose with concrete numbers, explicit contradictions and a measurement critique, so the production parser, chunker, evidence extractor and claim verifier run over realistic input instead of placeholder snippets. Replace docs/*.md and the metadata here to evaluate a real corpus; the schema is the contract.

sources.title: Longitudinal Evidence on Remote Work and Team Output
sources.snippet: A four-year panel of 4,200 knowledge workers found individual output up 12 percent and cross-team collaboration down 18 percent.

sources.title: A Meta-Analysis of 27 Remote Work Studies Finds No Reliable Productivity Effect
sources.snippet: Pooling 27 studies and 41,000 workers gives a standardised mean difference of 0.04, with an interval that crosses zero.

sources.title: A Field Experiment in a Call Centre: Task Interdependence Decides the Effect
sources.snippet: Remote agents resolved 8 percent more independent cases per hour and 4 percent fewer coordination-heavy cases per hour.

sources.title: Industry Survey Report: Remote Work and Output
sources.snippet: Managers at 380 firms estimated a 20 percent increase in output and a 35 percent increase in satisfaction after moving to remote work.

sources.title: Measurement Problems in Remote Work Research
sources.snippet: Nineteen of 27 studies relied on self-report and 41 percent used hours logged as the outcome, which is an input rather than output.
